reviewers.agent: claude general-purpose subagents, independent contexts. Two ran in PARALLEL on scoped diffs (the blankline checker + ADR + rule + CONTRIBUTING; the symbolcheck module + docs-accuracy rule + quickstart + README), then four sequential rounds over each fix delta. Each was given the engine:claude rule bodies verbatim, the skills-policy review charter, and a scoped warden-packaged diff. Reviews executed rather than read: the quickstart was extracted from its fences and run end to end, mermaid sequences were rendered under two mermaid versions to test an escaping hazard, and the test-cache hole was reproduced with a live violating file.

claude general-purpose subagent, separate context; every round was instructed to refute its own findings before reporting and each returned an explicit refuted list alongside its findings — among them the vacuity floor, allowlist shadowing, receiverTypes false passes, and the &reg mermaid escaping hazard, all probed and cleared. The 2,307-line formatting sweep was verified mechanically by the orchestrator instead (0 deletions, every swept file byte-identical after stripping blank lines, -fix idempotent) and excluded from agent review as unreadable at that size.

records.finding: [r1] The repo-wide guard can return a CACHED PASS while a tracked file violates the rule, so the enforcement claim made in ADR-0014, CONTRIBUTING and the rule body overstates the mechanism. The guard reaches files through `git ls-files`; Go's test cache keys on files the run OPENED, and a newly added file was opened by no cached run.
records.evidence: With a violating tracked file present, `go test ./...` reported `ok (cached)`; the same tree with -count=1 reported FAIL naming the file:line. ci-go.sh ran `go test ./...` and setup-go restores GOCACHE across runs.
records.reason: scripts/ci-go.sh's test mode now passes -count=1, repairing test/blankline, test/licensehdr and test/symbolcheck at once. Reproduced and re-verified after the fix.

records.finding: [r1] The single instance the rule cites as its justification was misdescribed: 'six consecutive `if vc.X, err = unescape(...)` guards' — five call unescape, the sixth calls strconv.ParseInt.
records.evidence: biz/baggage.go:142 `if vc.Money.Amount, err = strconv.ParseInt(fields[5], 10, 64); err != nil`.
records.reason: Corrected — and corrected twice more (r4, r5) before it described all six guards truthfully.

records.finding: [r1] The one-line-block exception's rationale misstated the mechanism: the package doc and ADR-0014 grouped it with the 'not a block' cases, but a one-line `if` IS block-bodied and is excluded by the line comparison instead. The cited example is also unreachable, since gofmt expands it.
records.evidence: blockBodied returns true for every *ast.IfStmt; the exclusion is `closing.Line == open.Line` in checkList. `gofmt -d` rewrites `if err != nil { return err }` into three lines.
records.reason: Both files describe the two mechanisms as two. The old wording was then found surviving in the exception list (r3) and a subtest name (r4) and swept.

records.finding: [r1] The repo-wide guard had no non-empty floor: a filtered checkout makes git ls-files return nothing, the loop runs zero times and the test passes green having parsed nothing.
records.evidence: run() returns an empty slice with a nil error; the test asserts only `len(found) > 0`. ci-go.sh exits 2 on zero modules for the same reason.
records.reason: Refuses under 100 tracked files. test/licensehdr, found to share the gap, got the same floor (r3).

records.finding: [r2] The quickstart did not work as written. `go mod tidy` sat in step 1, before main.go exists, so it added no requires; step 4's `go run .` failed with five 'replaced but not required' errors. The page's opening promise was false for a reader following the steps.
records.evidence: Executed verbatim: step 1 tidy emits 'matched no packages'; step 4 fails on prometheus, biz, emit, registry and promhttp. Running tidy after step 3 resolves all five.
records.reason: Tidy moved to step 4, with a sentence saying a replace is not a require. Verified by running the page in strict step order, and the output still matches section 5 byte-for-byte.

records.finding: [r2] The rule body claimed a mechanical slice covering materially more than it did: a backticked selector written as a call with arguments was never scanned, because only a bare trailing '()' was stripped. 16 references went unchecked and two governed docs contributed zero selectors.
records.evidence: scanProse used strings.TrimSuffix(raw, "()") and qualifiedRE is $-anchored, so `emit.WithFlushInterval(d)` never matched. CONTRIBUTING repeated the overstatement.
records.reason: Rather than narrow the claim, stripCall now removes a trailing argument list, closing the gap. Proven by renaming a newly-covered symbol and watching the named failure.

records.finding: [r2] The package doc's 'not covered, by decision' list omitted the largest gap and implied call forms were handled.
records.evidence: 'A trailing "()" is stripped ... so `vc.Validate()` reads as a method reference' against TrimSuffix removing exactly two characters.
records.reason: The doc now says a trailing call is stripped arguments and all, and that arguments are never parsed.

records.finding: [r2] A comment carried dated review provenance and a README line number, both excluded by ADR-0014, and the line reference no longer resolved.
records.evidence: '(docs-accuracy, README.md:204, 2026-08-30)'; README.md:204 is a blank line at the commit that introduced it.
records.reason: Removed; the substantive point about go doc semantics kept.

records.finding: [r2] The Next section invoked a bare `shortfall` binary the reader has no documented way to obtain, on a page that had just explained the CLI cannot be installed from a private module.
records.evidence: The page's own step 2 parenthetical against an unqualified `shortfall impact` invocation.
records.reason: Runs from the clone like step 2, with go install named as the post-flip form.

records.finding: [r3] stripCall — the only new logic in that commit — had no test. Reverting it to the old TrimSuffix left the whole suite green, and the repo-wide guard could not catch it either, since reverting only DROPS references and the floor is a minimum.
records.evidence: Mutation: `text := strings.TrimSuffix(raw, "()")` → package green.
records.reason: Five named cases; three redden on exactly that mutation. A sixth was added in r4 for the suffix guard.

records.finding: [r3] The -count=1 change left this doc quoting the old command.
records.evidence: '`scripts/ci-go.sh test` is a plain `go test ./...`' against the script's `go test -count=1 ./...`.
records.reason: Quotes the current command; the -race point it was making is unchanged.

records.finding: [r3] The comment justifying the cache-disable understated its own cost by an order of magnitude.
records.evidence: 'The whole tree tests in a few seconds' against a measured ~25s uncached.
records.reason: States both numbers, ~25s against ~2.5s. Independently re-measured at 23.2s/2.5s.

records.finding: [r3] The corrected DecodeVC note claimed the six bodies are 'identical and only the decoder differs'. They carry six different messages.
records.evidence: biz/baggage.go:126-148 — six distinct fmt.Errorf messages.
records.reason: Corrected — and corrected again in r4 and r5 before it was true.

records.finding: [r3] Fixing the one-line-block rationale left the OLD rationale in the exception list two lines away, and in the inline comment on the line implementing the skip. Same split in ADR-0014.
records.evidence: 'no closing brace of its own to break after' against the corrected 'braces share a line'.
records.reason: Each file gives one account. The last copy, in a subtest name, was swept in r4.

records.finding: [r3] ref.text's field comment still described the pre-stripCall normalization.
records.evidence: 'the raw text without a trailing "()"' against text := stripCall(raw).
records.reason: Describes any trailing call.

records.finding: [r3] Two ALL-CAPS emphases were added to comments, which ADR-0014 forbids.
records.evidence: 'opens at the LAST unmatched "("' and 'IS block-bodied'.
records.reason: Rewritten without emphasis.

records.finding: [r3] test/licensehdr was the last tree guard without a non-empty floor, sharing the filtered-checkout vacuity the sibling fix names.
records.evidence: It asserts only `len(missing) > 0` over the same git ls-files helper.
records.reason: Same floor as its siblings.

records.finding: [r4] The DecodeVC note was wrong again in a new way: 'return a wrapped error naming the field' — the strconv.ParseInt guard uses %q on the raw field and never passes err on, so its error is not unwrappable.
records.evidence: biz/baggage.go:142-144 `fmt.Errorf("biz: biz.vc amount %q", fields[5])` against five siblings wrapping with %w.
records.reason: Rewritten from the code rather than paraphrase: all six decode a field and return a zero ValueContext with an error identifying it. Verified clause by clause against all six guards.

records.finding: [r4] stripCall's contract has two halves and only one was pinned. Deleting the HasSuffix guard — the 'closes the string' clause its doc comment makes load-bearing — left the package green.
records.evidence: Without the guard, `emit.New(cfg) then more` strips to `emit.New` and resolves.
records.reason: A named case reddens on exactly that mutation and on nothing else in stripCall.

records.finding: [r5] The name paragraph said a loss-only word 'would have been wrong for three of the five legs'. The report has four legs and a trust line, as the same section says twice.
records.evidence: README 'four legs and a trust line out' and 'the other four defensible'; money.md, c4-l3 and CONTRIBUTING agree.
records.reason: The countable claim was removed entirely after a third attempt at it failed (r6).

records.finding: [r5] The sentence after the corrected note enumerated the varying dimensions as 'the decoder and the error's wording', omitting that the amount guard drops the cause — the very thing that made an earlier version wrong.
records.evidence: The %q guard's error is not unwrappable to the strconv.NumError.
records.reason: Both axes named.

records.finding: [r5] The new clearance row was marked ✅ for an item its own evidence cell said is not done, with no date, searcher, tool or queries, in a table whose other ✅ rows cite something checkable in the tree.
records.evidence: '✅ first pass only | ... a first pass is not clearance' against sibling rows citing a gitleaks scan, go.mod, SECURITY.md.
records.reason: Carries 👤 like its sibling clearance rows, dated and attributed as founder-reported, stating plainly it is not reproducible here.

records.finding: [r6] The corrected denominator introduced a wrong numerator: 'deferred, unrealized and customer impact are none of them a loss figure' — the table row fifteen lines above is literally named Unrealized loss, and the engine computes it net of recovery so that what remains is loss.
records.evidence: README:43 '| **Unrealized loss** | ... | estimate |'; engine/unrealized.go computes `short * aov * (1 - recovery)`.
records.reason: The tally is gone. The paragraph makes the point it existed for — the word carries recoverability, deferred value being the case in point — and counts nothing.

records.finding: [r6] Moving the clearance row from ✅ to 👤 made the header census off by one: it still said two items are personal actions where there are now three besides the flip.
records.evidence: Three 👤 founder rows (Go ecosystem, trademark, employer IP) plus the flip, against 'two items are personal actions'.
records.reason: Header says three; verified by count.

records.finding: [r6] The header note said the clearance row was 'added 2026-08-31'; within this branch it was re-marked, not added, in a file whose title is 'state of record'.
records.evidence: git diff shows the row present at the prior commit as a modified line.
records.reason: Says the row dates from that day, true either way.
